title: What a chart can tell me
text: A chart makes some patterns easier to see, but it also reflects a series of choices. Which observations belong in the plot? What belongs on each axis? Which differences deserve attention?

title: What a chart can tell me
text:
One choice that matters
In a comparison of income and life expectancy, a logarithmic income axis changes the spacing of the values. That can help reveal patterns that are difficult to see when a few large values stretch the scale.

title: What a chart can tell me
section: What I still need to ask
text:
What I still need to ask
A visible association does not explain why the pattern exists. Before moving from description to explanation, I need to think about the research question, the data, and possible alternative explanations.
My next step is to describe the plot in one careful sentence, then write down a question it cannot answer.

A project I’m developing

Comparing life expectancy across countries
COURSE PROJECT · IN PROGRESS
Question. How does life expectancy vary with income across countries in a given year?
Approach. Use R to explore the historical Gapminder data and make a clearly labeled visualization.
What I’m learning. Choosing the year, scale, and unit of analysis changes what readers can see. An association in a plot is a starting point for questions, not evidence of a causal effect.

title: Travel & places
text:
What I learned

Travel is most rewarding when you arrive with curiosity rather than expectations. The moments I remember most from Oxford were often the ones I never planned for.
Living and studying in another country taught me to pay closer attention to how history, culture, and daily life shape the way people think and communicate.
I learned that there is value in slowing down, observing, and asking questions. Understanding a place comes less from seeing famous landmarks and more from listening to the people who call it home.

title: Academic interests & research
text:
Projects I’m developing

When Words Become Risk: War Rhetoric and Safe-Haven Currency Markets
UNDERGRADUATE HONORS THESIS · IN PROGRESS
Question How does war threat rhetoric influence safe-haven currency markets?
Description This project examines the relationship between geopolitical rhetoric and foreign exchange markets. Rhetoric data are merged with CHF, JPY, and USD exchange-rate data obtained from FRED and benchmarked against the Caldara and Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk (GPR) Index. Regression analysis is used to estimate the effects of geopolitical rhetoric on exchange-rate returns, while GARCH models are employed to assess its impact on exchange-rate volatility.

Completed Projects

The Angeleno Outlook: Ten Years of Change in How Angelenos View the LA Region and their Place in It
AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR PUBLIC OPINION RESEARCH (AAPOR) PANEL PRESENTATION · COMPLETED
Chhandosi Roy Ph.D., Alecco Walli, Maricia Marquez (Center for the Study of Los Angeles)
Description: Used twelve years of Angeleno Poll data to examine how institutional trust, economic perceptions, and community belonging shape regional pessimism in Los Angeles.
Approach: Applied logistic regression modeling and predicted probability analysis to evaluate drivers of public opinion trends across demographic groups.
Findings: • Trust in city government and perceptions of economic disparity appear to be stronger drivers of regional pessimism than personal financial outlook. • Future research should include more longitudinal measures of attitudes toward institutions essential to a functioning democracy. • Additional study is needed on the role of messaging and information sources in shaping public perceptions.
